title: Surface Atomic Defects and Self-Regulated CO Adsorption on Cu(111): Insights from High-Resolution Scanning Probe Microscopy
content: Recent advances in high-resolution scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) have enabled the direct visualization and manipulation of individual molecules and atoms in real space [1-4]. In this work, we investigated the adsorption of CO molecules on Cu(111) surfaces. The system was constructed using a CO-functionalized tip mounted on a qPlus sensor to perform STM/AFM imaging of CO molecules adsorbed on Cu(111) surfaces [5]. Experiments were conducted using a CreaTecTM STM/AFM system under ultrahigh vacuum conditions at two temperatures, 4.8 and 77.6 K. The qPlus sensor had a resonance frequency of 30 KHz with a spring constant k = 1,800 N/m, and the quality factor in our measurement was about 20,000.
